task: Cost-reduction investigation: verify (against real, current behavior/docs - not assumption) whether Claude Code Remote Routines can run as fresh, non-context-accumulating sessions (create_new_session_on_fire) instead of bound to a persistent session (self-bind/persistent_session_id, how every one of our current recurring check-ins works). A background research agent claimed Routines are always 'fresh, no context bloat' - that contradicts what we've directly observed (Sam's own persistent-session-bound check-in has accumulated 600k+ tokens of context over one day). If fresh-session-per-fire is real and would actually cut cost without losing anything (our protocol is already stateless - all real state lives in git/GitHub, not conversation memory), propose how to migrate our triggers to it. Report findings plainly either way, including anything you're not fully certain about.

Jordan.output: Confirmed real: create_new_session_on_fire is a genuine, working Routine mode that spawns a fresh, non-accumulating session per fire (proven via list_triggers - the Daily Morning Brief and Kanye ticket-watch triggers show a distinct session_id on each fire, no persistent_session_id). Root cause of the cost growth: cache reads are NOT free (~0.1x input price on Sonnet 5, ~$0.20/1M), and a persistent-session-bound trigger resends+re-reads-from-cache its ENTIRE accumulated history every fire, so per-fire cost grows roughly linearly with prior fires (total cost grows ~quadratically over time). My own session confirms this: 8.13M cache-read tokens, ~$4.52 total after ~6h of a 2h-cadence trigger. A fresh-session trigger's cost per fire stays roughly constant instead, since there is no growing tail to resend - and our protocol is already git/issue-#1-based state, so nothing is lost. Real tradeoff to flag: fresh-session fires would no longer land in this ongoing chat thread (only visible via git/issue #1 or completion notifications) - a genuine behavior change, not just a cost one, so I did not silently convert my own trigger; proposing it on issue #1 for a decision instead. Applied the simple, already-decided part of the cost directive (bumped my own trigger 2h->6h) directly.
